rows.before: PendingEdit kind list included `school_name` and the `player_name` kind wrote to THREE offsets per the PLAYER_NAME_OFFSETS array: body 0x47E (10 bytes, labelled '§22 canonical authoritative'), body 0x1149C (22 bytes, labelled 'character record per-display copy'), and body 0x114BA (10 bytes, labelled '§12.1 secondary cached copy'). The school_name kind wrote to two offsets via SCHOOL_NAME_OFFSETS: body 0x114B2 + body 0x115B2. The header comment described the three player-name writes as 'mirror copies'.
rows.after: PendingEdit list updated to `player_name` (write only to body 0x1149C), `shop_name` (write only to body 0x114B2; renamed from school_name to reflect submission #16's empirical evidence that the field holds the SHOP name, not a school name), and a NEW `town_name` kind (write only to body 0x47E; previously this offset was being clobbered by player_name writes). PLAYER_NAME_OFFSETS / SCHOOL_NAME_OFFSETS arrays replaced with single-offset constants PLAYER_NAME_OFFSET / SHOP_NAME_OFFSET / TOWN_NAME_OFFSET. Each edit kind zero-fills the full readable field width (22 bytes for player at 0x1149C, 32 bytes for shop at 0x114B2, 22 bytes for town at 0x47E) so longer prior content is wiped, but caps user input at the in-game name-entry limits (5/6/5 chars respectively). The pre-step-258 dead-code write to body 0x115B2 is removed — that offset has been empty (zeros) in every v2.31 corpus save we've checked. The header comment block was rewritten to walk through the submission #16 evidence trail that refuted step-252's 'three mirrors of one field' interpretation.
rows.reason: Submission #16 (Harry Potter playthrough where the user gave DIFFERENT names for player / shop / town: player=WEASLEY, shop=Shop Weasleys, town=HOGSMEADE) proved that body 0x47E / 0x1149C / 0x114BA are NOT mirrors — they're independent fields. Step-252's editor was clobbering the town name on every player rename and corrupting the middle of the shop name field (0x114BA is at offset +8 INSIDE the 0x114B2 shop-name field). This is the bug fix.

submission_16_evidence.summary: Submission #16 is a Harry Potter-themed playthrough where the user gave DIFFERENT strings for player / shop / town, which refutes step-252's 'three mirror copies of one field' interpretation.

offsets_at_slot_A_body.0x114BA (alleged 'secondary player name': 20 00 57 00 65 00 61 00 73 00 6c 00 65 00 79 00 73 00 -> ' Weasleys' (NOT a separate field — bytes +8..+25 of the 0x114B2 shop-name field, just an offset misread)
offsets_at_slot_A_body.0x115B2 (alleged 'documented mirror'): 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 ff 00 00 00 00 -> all zeros (NOT used by any save in our corpus)

submission_16_evidence.cross_reference_tyler_test_save: C:/Users/Tyler/Desktop/Hack/DeSmuME-VS2019-x64-Release (1)/Battery/Saves for hacking/tongari_en.dsv — body 0x47E reads 'FUNNY' and body 0x1149C reads 'タイラ', both player-named fields. This is the trap that fooled step-252 into thinking they were mirrors: Tyler used the same name for player and town in his test save, so every offset trivially matched and the 'mirror' interpretation looked correct. Submission #16's distinct-name playthrough was the empirical test that broke the false interpretation.
